source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "ដំណាំសណ្តែកដី" (Peanut / Groundnut Cultivation handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, 2008, produced under Loan 2022-CAM(SF) (an ADB-financed project; the cover names a livelihood/agriculture-improvement program under this loan). Uploaded as a 14-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source B for crop/peanut in this knowledge base (Source A was a shorter ECOSORN leaflet processed in Batch 42).
text: Harvest timing can be judged by several field signs: leaf color turning from green toward yellow; roughly 50% of leaves per plant showing yellowing; and pod shells changing from a lighter color to a darker, dry brown tone, with the shell surface becoming more veined/wrinkled and hardened. If heavy rain is expected within a day or two of the crop reaching maturity, the source advises harvesting promptly, since delayed harvest risks pod rot and increased damage from soil-dwelling pests (e.g. termites/ants) attacking pods underground; leaving mature pods in wet soil for too long can also cause seeds to sprout in the ground. Harvested plants should be allowed to dry before pulling if the soil is muddy or wet at pulling time. Reported yield potential for peanut is roughly 600-2,500 kg/ha (in-shell) within one hectare.
